transcript:
Header: 2026-12-09 10:00 UTC | Duration: 60 mins | Attendees: Maya Patel, Jonah Li, Priya Singh, Alex Gomez, Taylor Reed, Samir Khan

Summary: quick run-through of messaging, then two dry-run demos (API + Dedicated failover), ended with objection handling practice and next steps.

[00:00] Maya (AE): okay hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, um, today's a short one - 60 minutes - focus on messaging and demo practice, please interrupt if things go off the rails.
[00:12] Priya (Enablement): hi hi, I sent the agenda earlier, we have a refreshed cost slide and a new routing diagram. we'll try two runs and then the objection roleplay.
[00:25] Jonah (SE): cool, I'll take the demo, Maya you'll do the intro messaging and then I'll walk through API, Dedicated, and the fallback.
[00:33] Maya: yup, quick reminder of the core message: production-first inference, predictable economics, unified API across hosted, dedicated, private. keep it short — customers often only remember 2–3 bullets.
[00:45] Alex (SE): quick q — are we emphasizing latency SLAs or cost savings first? for enterprise buyers they ask SLAs a lot.
[00:52] Maya: good — lead with reliability/latency for enterprise, cost/performance for dev-first leads. example opener: "we help teams cut per-token cost while keeping predictable p99 latency and simple dev workflows."
[01:08] Taylor: can we call out KV cache and batching in the pitch? some customers care about concrete levers.
[01:15] Jonah: yeah mention automatic prefix/KV caching and smart batching, but avoid too many deep technical words in the first 30s — second slide is where we level up.
[01:30] Priya: note — sometimes the term "KV cache" gets misheard, some docs spelled it K V cache in earlier decks, updated that.
[01:38] Maya: okay moving into demo run 1 — Jonah?

DEMO RUN 1 (API focus)
[02:00] Jonah: starting share screen — opening the Redwood API quickstart, sample app, we'll show a chat request, streaming responses, then switch to a long-tail prompt to show batching benefits.
[02:18] Jonah: request 1 — user asks for product spec summary, model is rwd-alpha-1 (fake name in practice), streaming tokens appear, latency ~120ms on this demo env (note: demo env not representative).
[02:35] Maya: callout — be explicit that metrics in GA are different; always prefaced with "demo environment, not SLA numbers".
[02:45] Jonah: right. now second example: large batch of concurrent requests — show how our runtime does continuous batching and maintains throughput. sometimes the transcript had "continuous batch thing" — avoid that phrase. say "continuous batching and KV cache reduces effective cost".
[03:12] Taylor: during the demo, when a customer asks about model ownership — how do we position model catalog vs BYO?
[03:20] Maya: say we host curated open models and Redwood-verified profiles; customers can also bring their own model for Dedicated and Private. emphasize the unified API consistent across modes.
[03:33] Alex: competitor knock — Anthropic says they have guardrails and safety, how do we answer?
[03:40] Priya: differentiator: we focus on production economics and operational controls; safety tooling is partnerable and we can show eval/regression tooling in Redwood Optimize. also mention rollout controls for gradual traffic shifts.
[03:58] Jonah: demo note — I flubbed the fallback example earlier, we should script it: show primary hosted model, then trigger a simulated capacity event and route to a compatible quantized variant on Dedicated.

DEMO RUN 2 (Dedicated + Fallback)
[05:00] Jonah: okay second run: start from Console, show per-route latency metrics, then trigger a simulated capacity constraint (demo toggle) — routing policy moves requests to Dedicated pool and then to a low-cost quantized variant.
[05:25] Maya: callout: this is where customers light up — show the routing policy UI and the automatic fallback rules. say "automatic fallback to compatible variants keeps apps online".
[05:38] Samir: quick interjection — do we show pricing numbers? sometimes legal/regional deals want ranges.
[05:45] Maya: give ballpark ranges and suggest "we'll share a tailored estimate after a quick baseline test" — avoid exact per-token commitments in first call.
[06:00] Jonah: showing trace: request path, KV cache hit, kernel selection note — sometimes the transcript earlier said "kernel elective" which is wrong, say "kernel selection for performance".
[06:22] Taylor: there's often a question on encryption/KMS — what's the one-liner?
[06:28] Priya: "Data is encrypted at rest and in transit; customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations available for Private deployments; audit logs and SOC 2 controls are standard for Dedicated and Private customers."
[06:40] Maya: highlight SSO/SAML, RBAC, and retention settings too.

OBJECTION ROLEPLAY
[08:00] Maya (playing skeptic): okay Alex, act like you're the security lead — "we need SOC 2 and customer-managed KMS, can you guarantee no exfil?"
[08:08] Alex (playing security): um, yeah, what's the guarantee on that — and what about data residency?
[08:15] Jonah (responding): we offer Private deployments for residency/air-gapped needs; for hosted and Dedicated we provide encryption in transit/at rest plus audit logs and integrations with customer KMS. also we have contract language for data handling.
[08:35] Maya: good — add that we do pen tests and can provide SOC 2 report under NDA. avoids too much legal-speak on first call.
[08:45] Samir: competitive, cost objection: "OpenAI cheaper for embeddings" — how to answer?
[08:52] Priya: acknowledge market differences, then pivot: "cost per token is one factor; operational predictability, throughput, and integration overhead often make Redwood more cost-effective at scale". give an example: batching+cache lowered our benchmarking customer costs by ~40% in long-tail workloads (say approximate).

messy bits / transcription quirks noted: sometimes Redwood product names in notes were written as "Redwood dedicate" or "Redwood privatee" — fix copy. also "K V cache" vs "KV cache".

RECENT PRACTICE RUN — SHORT SCRIPT
[10:30] Jonah: script: 1) 30s opener — value prop; 2) 60s architecture slide; 3) 3-min demo showing API chat and routing failover; 4) 30s security/next steps. let's run it once full speed.
[10:45] (fast runthrough, stumbles at 2:15 on the fallback step)
[13:05] Maya: pause — on the fallback line, say "automatic fallback to compatible quantized variants keeps your app online with graceful degradation" not "we just change models" which sounds flippant.
[13:20] Taylor: also practice the "we'll share benchmarks" line — customers want numbers early; say "we'll run a quick benchmark with your workload and share numbers".

CLOSING
[55:30] Maya: wrap-up — good practice, Priya will update slides and battlecard, Jonah will record the clip, I'll send the follow-up email with assets and suggested runbook for SEs. next enablement scheduled 2026-12-20 for competitive deep dive.
[55:47] Priya: adding note — update Confluence page and tag the enablement channel.
[56:02] Jonah: minor ask — can we get a short 1-page cheat sheet for PMs that covers "when to choose Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted"?
[56:12] Maya: yes I'll add that to action items.

End transcript.
